- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate during mean-reversion phases; adjust downward by 1–3% if recent 7-day average is below 30-day average.
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., 70→75) and fail to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use exponential decay to smooth out overshoot.
- Lagged response to true price movements: delay correction by 1–2 days if true price rises sharply; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true peak.
- High variance in short-term (1–7 day) forecasts; use 30-day moving average as baseline for smoothing.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history; if last 5 days are trending up, don’t assume continuation beyond 30-day horizon.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 5–10% to avoid runaway bias.
- For low volatility periods, reduce forecast spread by 20–30% to avoid overconfidence in noise.
